text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA

- American car maker Ford will come to Russia's market through the "back door" by launching a new Ford production line near the Belarussian capital, Minsk. Belarus enjoys low Russian customs duties on cars made on its territory. High Russian import duties have held back a flood of foreign cars so far.

- Peace in Abkhazia, the breakaway region of Georgia, will evidently last till September. The mandate of Russian peacekeepers in the region expired on Thursday, but they will stay there at least another month.
- Belarussian leaders seem to have ignored Russian President Boris Yeltsin's extremely firm reaction to the arrest of a Russian television crew there.
- A new round of the bitter row over the sale of Russia's state telecoms company broke out on Thursday after media tycoon Vladimir Gusinsky announced his intention to sue the buyer for defamation.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- The uproar over Russia's biggest telecoms company will develop further after Vladimir Potanin, head of Uneximbank, expressed his intention to bid in a second tender for 24 percent of Svyazinvest, which is open to Russian investors only.

- The fate of 49 percent of Sukhoi Log gold deposit shares will be decided by its shareholders at the end of August. Irkutsk region administration expects the return of Australian Star Technology to the auction.
- The government is planning to reduce the number of Russia's airlines, which will have federal status.
SEVODNYA

- Special health inspectors will be monitoring all the dispatches of imported meat from EU countries beginning from August 15, says a top government official in connection with the measures Russia is taking to prevent the penetration of British beef, possibly tainted by mad cow disease, into Russian markets.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Confrontation between Russia and Belarus is growing into a media war.
- President Boris Yeltsin tops a ranking of Russia's most influential politicians in July, according to a survey. He is followed by Anatoly Chubais and Viktor Chernomyrdin.

- The leader of Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya, Aslan Maskhadov and President Boris Yeltsin are ready to meet to discuss a wide-ranging pact, under which the Chechens expect to receive wider political autonomy.
- Russia's state-owned oil company Rosneft is pulling out of a $1-billion deal to develop a major Caspian oil deposit with LUKoil and Azeri state oil firm SOCAR.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA

- Russia's relief space crew, scheduled to leave for the Mir station on August 5, will be paid $100 for every day aboard the crippled station and $1,000 for every spacewalk, a space official is quoted as saying. Their mission is scheduled to last 194 days, involving at least six spacewalks.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko arrested a Russian television crew to intimidate Belarussian journalists.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
